meta.rule: A question moves to 'answered' only when the answer has a source link or a reproducible check. 'We cannot know yet' is a legitimate answer and is recorded as such.
meta.status: Twenty-four questions. 10 are answered. 14 are open, and each one names the specific document, dashboard or decision that would close it.
meta.how_to_read: The blocking column is the useful one. A blocking question means work that depends on it is guesswork until it is answered.

questions.question: Did each submitted link land on the product the owner meant to send readers to?
questions.what_we_have: All five submitted short links reached a live listing on an earlier pass on 2026-11-20, with arrival ASINs and titles transcribed: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z. Two later passes the same day reached no listing at all — all five short links returned https://www.amazon.com/. The five direct /dp/ URLs were re-opened and every page title matched the record. See FLG-028.
questions.what_is_missing: Two things, and they are different. First, the owner's intended ASIN: the supplied codes are nine characters and lowercase, the observed ASINs are ten and uppercase, and intent cannot be read off a redirect that behaves differently on different passes. Second, a stable destination for the short link form itself.
questions.how_to_close: In the Associates dashboard, open SiteStripe for each product and copy the tagged link for the exact ASIN intended. Record both values side by side, as the register does.
questions.blocking: yes — the product-record fields depend on it

questions.question: Why did one link fail to resolve at all?
questions.what_we_have: P-04 (link.amazon/B0c8moW59) failed three times in an earlier session, resolved once on 2026-11-20 to B0DHZTCNR5, and on later passes the same day reached only the Amazon homepage like the other four. Every short link has now shown at least two arrival behaviours.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing for the /dp/ destination, which was re-confirmed directly. What remains unknown is why the short-link form returns different pages across passes, so no claim is made about the cause and none is inferred.
questions.how_to_close: Closed for the destination on 2026-11-20. The cause of the earlier failures is recorded as unexplained rather than diagnosed.
questions.answer: The direct /dp/ URL resolves and opens a ThermoMaven digital meat thermometer, which is a different product category from the three air fryers and is treated as such on the site. The short link is not a stable route to it.
questions.evidence: Direct observation, 2026-11-20: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DHZTCNR5 returns the ThermoMaven listing; https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 returned https://www.amazon.com/ on a later pass (FLG-028).

questions.question: Are clicks attributed to shopnow047c-20?
questions.what_we_have: No Amazon link on the site carries ?tag=shopnow047c-20 yet. Program Policies 2(a)-(b) require a Special Link to use the Associates ID; a Special Link generated in Associates Central and validated by one test click has not been recorded.
questions.what_is_missing: Confirmation from an Associates report that a click was recorded against the tag. No dashboard access is available to this build.
questions.how_to_close: Click one link on the live site, then open Reports → Orders in the Associates dashboard and look for the click against the tag.
questions.blocking: yes — until this is confirmed the site may be sending traffic that does not pay

questions.question: Should the site show prices?
questions.what_we_have: Program Policies 2(b) permits prices and availability only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where it arrives via Creators API or PA API (SRC-02). Neither is connected.
questions.what_is_missing: A decision, and if the answer is yes, API credentials.
questions.how_to_close: Either apply for API access and render Amazon-served prices only, or keep prices off the site. Both are compliant; a copied or scraped price is not.
questions.blocking: no — the site is compliant without prices
questions.answer: No price, star rating, review count or stock status appears anywhere on this site. Every buy button sends the reader to Amazon, where that data is served live.

questions.question: Is the disclosure in the right place, and does it say enough?
questions.what_we_have: A disclosure strip sits under the masthead on every page, above the content, and is repeated in the footer. It states the Associates relationship in the sentence the Operating Agreement requires.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing structural. The FTC frames placement as a judgement about prominence, and says the closer the disclosure is to the recommendation, the better (SRC-03).
questions.how_to_close: Answered by the sources. Reviewing the wording remains an owner decision, not a gap.
questions.answer: Above the fold on every page, repeated in the footer, and reinforced with a 'Paid links' label next to it. The FTC guidance explicitly treats a bare 'affiliate link' label as possibly insufficient, which is why the strip carries a full sentence as well as the label.

questions.question: Two of the five products are thermometers. Do they belong on this site?
questions.what_we_have: P-04 and P-05 resolve to meat thermometers. Three products are air fryers.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing factual. The question is editorial positioning, and a decision was taken.
questions.how_to_close: Answered by deciding to publish thermometers as their own category rather than as a fifth air fryer.
questions.answer: Yes, in their own section. A probe is a measuring tool that moves between appliances, and it is the cheapest way to make an air fryer predictable. Filing it under Air Fryers would have been inaccurate.

questions.question: Which topics are worth writing next?
questions.what_we_have: Ten guides on editorial hypotheses: shape, dual-zone, capacity, cleanup, small kitchens, multi-function appliances, thermometers, seasonal hosting, meal-prep geometry and holiday side-dish capacity.
questions.what_is_missing: Search data. No Search Console property is connected, so no topic has been chosen from measured demand.
questions.how_to_close: Verify the property, submit the sitemap, wait two to four weeks, then pick the next topic from the queries that actually appear.
questions.blocking: no — but every further guide is a guess until it is answered

questions.question: Who is the author, and why should a reader trust them?
questions.what_we_have: No named author. The site's claim is narrow and checkable: the links were opened and the listings read.
questions.what_is_missing: A person, a biography that describes work that actually happened, and a decision about whether to publish under a name at all.
questions.how_to_close: Name an editor and write an accurate bio, or keep the publication anonymous and stop implying personal expertise. Both are honest; the second is weaker for search.
questions.blocking: partly — it caps how much authority the site can claim

questions.question: What does each category actually pay?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. Commission rates are set per category in the Associates programme and are visible in the account.
questions.what_is_missing: The account's current rate card.
questions.how_to_close: Open the Commission Income Statement in the Associates dashboard and record the rate for Home & Kitchen furniture and appliance categories.
questions.blocking: no — but no revenue estimate can be made without it, and none is offered

questions.question: Is there an analytics endpoint that can be switched on lawfully?
questions.what_we_have: A self-hosted collector (_analytics/endpoint.py) and a cookie-free client that records five defined events. Both are inert.
questions.what_is_missing: A host for the collector, a retention statement, and a lawful basis for processing IP addresses.
questions.how_to_close: Deploy the collector to a host you control, set retention, edit the privacy page with the specifics, then point the client at it.
questions.blocking: yes — measurement work waits on it

questions.question: Can this site be indexed, given that it lives on a repository subpath?
questions.what_we_have: Every internal link is relative, so the site works at /Affil1/. A sitemap, a robots file and canonical URLs are generated by the build and checked on every run.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing technical. Whether Google has crawled it is a different question, answered by Search Console.
questions.how_to_close: Answered in the repository; crawling confirmation is Q-07's dependency.
questions.answer: Yes. The build refuses to emit a root-absolute internal link, and the Pages workflow fails if the sitemap and the built pages disagree.

questions.question: Does the site make any claim it cannot support?
questions.what_we_have: A checker that fails the build on currency figures, star ratings, review counts, stock phrases, sales superlatives and any first-person testing verb.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing automated. The check catches patterns, not meaning, so a human read is still required before publishing new prose.
questions.how_to_close: Answered by the automated rules plus editorial review; it is a standing control rather than a one-off.
questions.answer: Not by construction. Product facts come only from transcribed listing titles; editorial notes describe what a stated feature changes, not a tested result.
questions.evidence: _tools/check.py BANNED rules; build fails on violation

questions.question: What if the owner never supplies the missing account data?
questions.what_we_have: A site that is compliant and complete without it: five checked links, eight guides, one comparison table.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing that blocks publication. Attribution and rates stay unconfirmed and are published as such.
questions.how_to_close: Answered by publishing the gap rather than waiting for it to close.
questions.answer: The site publishes anyway. Every unconfirmed item is on the Flagged for Review page with the source needed to close it, so the absence is visible rather than hidden.

questions.question: Are the product links Special Links in the sense the Operating Agreement means?
questions.what_we_have: Program Policies 2(a) requires Special Links to use the Associates ID; 2(b) requires the tag as a URL parameter. No product link carries the tag yet; buy buttons are plain listing links, marked sponsored and labelled as listing sources.
questions.what_is_missing: Confirmation that the tag is registered and that clicks from this site are being recorded. That can only come from the account.
questions.how_to_close: One click from the live site, then the Orders report. The same test closes Q-03.

questions.question: Is there any traffic, and where would it come from?
questions.what_we_have: No measurement of any kind has been collected. The campaign ledger is deliberately empty.
questions.what_is_missing: Analytics (Q-10) and Search Console (Q-07).
questions.how_to_close: Do not forecast. Switch on measurement, then read it.

questions.question: Should one repository serve two competing editions of the same site?
questions.what_we_have: It did: a generated edition at the root and a hand-written edition under crisp/ plus a set of duplicate root pages. They described the same five products and could compete with each other in search.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing factual. This was a duplication problem with a clear answer.
questions.how_to_close: Answered on 2026-11-20 by consolidating into one canonical edition and archiving the other with noindex.
questions.answer: One site is indexed. The root build is canonical, the duplicate pages are archived under _archive/legacy-2026-11-20/ with a noindex tag, and the sitemap lists only the canonical pages.
questions.evidence: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, _archive/legacy-2026-11-20/ (noindex meta on every archived page)

questions.question: Is a github.io subpath the right long-term home?
questions.what_we_have: The site is served at karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil1/ and every link is relative so the subpath works.
questions.what_is_missing: A domain decision. A custom domain would need DNS, a CNAME file and canonical URLs rewritten in one place.
questions.how_to_close: Decide whether to buy a domain. The build has one constant for the site URL, so the change is small when the decision is made.
questions.blocking: no — but it constrains brand and link equity later

questions.question: What may a page say about a product beyond its listing title?
questions.what_we_have: Editorial rule: a stated feature may be explained in terms of what it changes for the cook, and nothing may be described as tested, measured or compared in use.
questions.what_is_missing: A written house style for the owner to approve or amend.
questions.how_to_close: Approve the rule as written on the About page, or amend it there.
questions.answer: Explain the trade, not the performance. 'Two independent drawers mean two temperatures at once' is a reading of a stated feature. 'Cooked evenly' would be a test claim and is banned by the checker.

questions.question: What may a buy button say when the site holds no price data?
questions.what_we_have: 'See it on Amazon' and 'Check it on Amazon', each followed by a line saying price and rating are shown on Amazon. No figure, no implied discount.
questions.what_is_missing: Owner sign-off on the wording. This is a compliance judgement, and the site is not the authority on it.
questions.how_to_close: Read the buttons against Program Policies 2(b) and the FTC's affiliate guidance; change the wording if it reads as a price claim.
questions.blocking: no — but it should be reviewed before paid traffic is sent

questions.question: How does the site capture readers without a backend?
questions.what_we_have: An RSS feed and a prominent link to it. No form, no email list, no third-party service.
questions.what_is_missing: A decision about email: a provider, a privacy notice, and a double opt-in flow.
questions.how_to_close: Choose a provider and publish the privacy terms, or commit to RSS and stop describing a newsletter as pending.

questions.question: Can the site show product photographs?
questions.what_we_have: Editorial illustrations generated for this publication, each labelled as an illustration and none presented as the product.
questions.what_is_missing: A permitted source of product imagery. Amazon product images come with licence conditions, and the Associates programme has its own rules about Program Content.
questions.how_to_close: Either obtain images through the permitted API, or commission photography of products actually bought and used. Until then, illustrations stay labelled.
questions.answer: No product photography is used. Every image is an illustration and says so on the page and in the image policy.

questions.question: What cadence can this publication actually sustain?
questions.what_we_have: Ten guides, written to one standard, each sourced from listing titles and general reasoning rather than tests.
questions.what_is_missing: A commitment from the owner. A cadence without an author is a wish.
questions.how_to_close: Choose one guide a fortnight or one a month, put it in the publishing workflow document, and hold to it.

questions.question: How big is the market this site is writing into — and does that change what is worth publishing?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing on this site depends on market size: guides are written from listing facts and general reasoning, and the queue says not to commission more until measurement lands (S-07).
questions.what_is_missing: Search volume per question theme. The only permitted source is a query report from a verified Search Console property (Q-11), not an estimate from a tool that will not show its method.
questions.how_to_close: Verify the Search Console property, submit the sitemap, wait for a sample of real queries, then rank future topics by observed demand instead of instinct.
questions.blocking: no — it informs topic choice (Q-07) but blocks nothing today

questions.question: What does a genuine self-test cost, and who authorises the spend?
questions.what_we_have: S-05 proposes buying one air fryer and publishing one tested comparison. The register currently has zero tested products and says so on every page.
questions.what_is_missing: A budget and a decision from the owner. Without one, 'tested' remains a word this site never uses, which is the honest position but also the ceiling on its usefulness.
questions.how_to_close: The owner sets a budget for one unit of the cheapest submitted product (or declines on the record); the purchase and the test protocol then enter the ledger with provenance.
questions.blocking: no — but it is the gate in front of S-05
